title: Progressive-disclosure skills documentation within the CLI
description:
# Progressive-disclosure skills documentation within the CLI

## Intent

Ship Limatus's own documentation the way the Agent Skills ecosystem itself
now recommends: a real CLI subcommand that prints the package's `SKILL.md`
content, so agents discover workflows/disambiguation live from the
installed tool instead of only through `--help`, and the installed skill
and the CLI's own docs can never drift apart (single source of truth).

This converges with a broader pattern that's formed since Anthropic
published the Agent Skills open standard in late 2025: MemNexus's `mx
agent-help`, the community-proposed `mycli skills` / `mycli skills <id>`
protocol, Mintlify serving `skill.md` on every docs site, and multiple
"AI-friendly CLI" writeups converging on the same shape -- a docs
subcommand an agent can call directly, distinct from `--help`.

## Why this over just good `--help`

`--help` is freeform and human-oriented -- it can't express command order,
prerequisites, which flags are required vs. optional, or "when you're
stuck between two similar commands, do X." Field data cited in the source
research (CLIWatch's benchmark) found agents forced to discover a complex
CLI through progressive `--help` alone completed 33% of tasks; a
skills-style subcommand mechanism recovered that to 50% and cut discovery
tokens roughly in half.

## Design, per the pattern's own field-tested lessons

- **A real subcommand, not a flag.** `limatus skill` (or similar), not
  `--agent-help`. Agents scan the command list; a flag is invisible to
  that scan the way a subcommand isn't.
- **Single source of truth.** The subcommand reads and prints the actual
  packaged `SKILL.md` (via `importlib.resources`, not a duplicated string
  literal) -- the installed skill and the CLI's live output are always the
  same file. Keep the YAML frontmatter intact when printing; agents
  tolerate it fine and it's what makes the identical file work whether
  it's read from a Claude Code skill install or piped from the CLI.
- **Advertise it explicitly.** A one-line pointer in the top-level
  `--help`/epilog, naming specific tools by name where that's shown to
  outperform a generic "AI agents:" phrasing.
- **Keep it lean.** Match the Agent Skills standard's own progressive-
  disclosure shape: a short name/description surfaced up front, full body
  on demand, SKILL.md itself under roughly 5,000 tokens.
- **Don't strip cross-references from regular `--help`.** Field data
  suggests agents use the skill dump for disambiguation/getting-unstuck,
  not first-pass discovery for a clear task -- `--help` still needs to
  carry enough to handle the common case on its own.

## Open questions

- Where does `limatus`'s own `SKILL.md` live once this exists -- is it the
  same file that gets installed as an actual Claude Code / Codex / Gemini
  CLI skill for *using* Limatus, or a separate CLI-reference doc? (The
  source material's implementation sketch assumes they're the same file --
  that's the whole point of the pattern, worth confirming it holds once
  Limatus has two capabilities (diagnose/options + the web usability
  loop) rather than one.)
- Does this ship as `limatus skill` (singular, whole-package dump) or
  `limatus skills` / `limatus skills <id>` (drill-down per capability),
  given Limatus will have at least two distinct capabilities once
  PPY-1cae29's web-usability loop lands?

## Relationship to the rest of Limatus

Sibling epic under the Limatus initiative. Depends on nothing else being
finished first, but is more useful once there's a real `SKILL.md` worth
serving -- reasonable to sequence after `LIM-2d43b1` (CLI/SDK decoupling)
has the CLI surface stable enough to document.
